+### Access Points and Multi-Region Access Points

+You can set `druid.storage.bucket` and `druid.indexer.logs.s3Bucket` to the ARN of an [S3 Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points.html) or a [Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPoints.html) instead of a bucket name. For example:

+Druid accepts both the `accesspoint/<name>` form that AWS documents and the `accesspoint:<name>` form, and converts the first to the second. In the `uris` and `prefixes` of an [S3 input source](../../ingestion/input-sources.md#s3-input-source), and in `druid.export.storage.s3.allowedExportPaths`, use the `accesspoint:<name>` form, for example `s3://arn:aws:s3::123456789012:accesspoint:abcdef0123456.mrap/path/to/file.json`.

+* Set `druid.storage.disableAcl=true` for a Multi-Region Access Point, and `druid.indexer.logs.disableAcl=true` if task logs use one. With ACLs enabled, Druid looks up the bucket owner using `GetBucketAcl`, which Multi-Region Access Points do not [support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MrapOperations.html). If ACLs are enabled for a Multi-Region Access Point ARN, Druid rejects the configuration before making any upload or move request. Regional Access Points support `GetBucketAcl`, so ACLs can stay enabled for them.
+* Druid sends requests for a regional Access Point to the Region in its ARN, even if that differs from `druid.s3.endpoint.signingRegion`. The ARN and the client must be in the same AWS partition.
+* Leave `druid.s3.enablePathStyleAccess` set to `false`. The AWS SDK rejects ARN buckets with path-style addressing.

+* Multi-Region Access Points do not support the multi-object `DeleteObjects` operation. Druid deletes objects behind a Multi-Region Access Point with one `DeleteObject` request per object, so killing segments and cleaning up task logs or durable storage sends more requests than with a bucket.

+* Requests to a Multi-Region Access Point are signed with SigV4A. If you use temporary credentials, request them from a regional AWS STS endpoint. Credentials from the global endpoint `sts.amazonaws.com` work only if you set its session tokens to be valid in all AWS Regions. See [Multi-Region Access Point restrictions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPointRestrictions.html).

+* Moving or archiving segments stored behind a Multi-Region Access Point is not supported. S3 accepts a Multi-Region Access Point only as the destination of `CopyObject`, not the source, so Druid fails these move requests. A Multi-Region Access Point can still be the target of a move from a bucket or regional Access Point.
The AWS SDK requires that a target region be specified.  You can set these by using the JVM system property `aws.region` or by setting an environment variable `AWS_REGION`.
